title: Recording: With A Little Luck by Wings | 1977
content:
Fair Carol, St John, US Virgin Islands
Producer: Paul McCartney
Engineers: Geoff Emerick, Mark Vigars

Wings continued recording the London Town song ‘With A Little Luck’ on 12 May 1977.

The session took place aboard the Fair Carol, a 105-foot yacht kitted out with studio equipment from the Record Plant in New York. It was initially moored in Francis Bay, St John, in the US Virgin Islands.

The backing track had been recorded by Paul and Linda McCartney on 9 May. On this day, Paul recorded a bass guitar overdub.

While listening back to the results, a National Park Service boat approached the Fair Carol. Police officers informed the captain that amplified music was prohibited in the bay after 10pm, and handed McCartney a citation with a $15 for doing so the previous night.

The Fair Carol’s Captain Carlo was uneasy at Wings’ propensity for smoking weed, and the police attention was enough for him to threaten to turn the electricity generators off at night. Due to the Caribbean heat, Wings were only able to work at night.

McCartney sought temporary refuge aboard a neighbouring catamaran, the Wanderlust, where he wrote a song that shared its name.

It’s actually a personal experience. What happened was that we were recording (we went out to the Virgin Islands to record an album called London Town) and we were on boats, in a little bay recording for a month. The captain of the boat that we were on was a little, sort of, heavier than the other captains – you know, he sort of took it a little more seriously – and at some stage we had a sort of argument with him, and I sort of said, ‘You know, we don’t need all this aggro stuff’, and we wanted to get off onto this other boat that happened to be in the harbour. These people had said we could come on this, and this boat happened to be called Wanderlust, so it became like a symbol of freedom to me, this catamaran, as it was, called Wanderlust. We only actually stayed one night on it, but it was like, after this hassling that this other fellow had given us, to get onto this boat was like freedom, you know, so the song for me is actually just carrying on the idea. You know, just head us out to sea and take us away from all these headaches, and just wanderlust kind of free.
Paul McCartney
Club Sandwich, 1982

A decision was made to move the Fair Carol, as well as the McCartneys’ rented boat, the El Toro, and the Samala, where the rest of Wings, studio engineer Geoff Emerick, and MPL’s management executive Alan Crowder stayed, to Waterlemon Bay, several miles east.

They left Francis Bay at 6pm. Wings jammed as they sailed to Waterlemon Bay, recording three pieces of music – ‘El Toro Passing’, ‘Untitled Jam’, and ‘Jam (On Arrival) At Watermelon [sic] Bay’.

Happily there were no more disasters and later in the week as the flotilla cruised across to Waterlemon Bay with the band jamming and recording, Alan Crowder had the look of Long John Silver as he waved his crutch from Samala to the main party on Fair Carol.
Mark Vigars
Club Sandwich #3, June/July 1977
